slides.speaker: S1

items: It is not an enforcement tool.

blocks.text: TRACE shows where flows and harms are heading, never where enforcement is weakest. No least-watched-route feature, no lowest-risk-corridor query, no ranking that helps anyone move product. That boundary is written into our engineering rules and enforced in code review.
CLAUDE.md · 'Design boundary (non-negotiable)' · committed before the first line of model code

slides.speaker: S2

blocks.to: Where does the harm land next?

blocks.text: Every other tool in this space answers the first question, for police. And every existing harm forecast is autoregressive — it predicts more of an epidemic a country already has. TRACE answers the second question, for public health, from outside: it forecasts harm in countries that have not had the epidemic yet, from the corridor that is about to open.

cues: This swap is the innovation claim. Make it the loudest sentence in your section.
'Autoregressive' is the word that separates us: everyone else forecasts more of what a country already has.
The first question serves enforcement. The second serves prevention.

slides.speaker: S3

blocks.text: The World Bank data is load-bearing, not decorative

items.title: Market mass
items.text: GDP, GDP per capita PPP, population set the size of every node in the gravity model.

items.title: Route friction
items.text: Governance, customs efficiency, port TEU, air traffic, trade openness explain why a flow takes one country and not its neighbour.

items.title: Vulnerability
items.text: Youth unemployment, NEET, poverty, Gini, health spend decide how badly a route's arrival hurts.

items.title: Validation targets
items.text: Homicide, HIV incidence, refugee flows are what the spillover hypothesis is tested against.

items.title: Detection-bias control
items.text: Rule of law and customs efficiency separate 'more drugs moving' from 'better at catching them'.

blocks.text: Remove the World Bank layer and the model has no market sizes, no friction, and no vulnerability. It stops being a model.

cues: This slide is aimed straight at the Graduate-track judge.
Role 5 is the one they won't expect — spend your time there.
If asked: governance codes are GOV_WGI_*.EST on source 3. The old CC.EST family is archive-only now. We found that by verifying against the live API.

slides.speaker: S3

blocks.text: Two models, and we report both

steps.title: PPML gravity
steps.text: Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood, the standard in trade economics. GDP, population, distance, contiguity, price gap.

steps.title: LightGBM hurdle
steps.text: (a) will this corridor be active next year, (b) how much moves if it is. Lagged volume, cultivation upstream, governance, logistics, OC Index, conflict.

steps.title: SHAP per corridor
steps.text: Every predicted shift comes with its drivers, in plain language, on the map.

blocks.text: Santos Silva & Tenreyro (2006) · Ke et al. (2017) · Lundberg & Lee (2017)

cues: The hurdle structure exists because most corridors are zero in most years. Say that — it shows you understand your own data.
SHAP is what turns a prediction into something a health ministry can act on.

slides.speaker: S3

blocks.text: Live Wire · the layer that beats the lag

items.title: Ingest
items.text: GDELT polled every 15 minutes, deduped, filtered to drug events worldwide.

items.title: Classify
items.text: Jev — TypeSafe's System One model — answers seven typed questions per article in one parallel pass, 70–500 ms: event type, drug, origin, transit, destination, size. Each answer carries a confidence score. Pinned to jev-1.13.0.

items.title: Flag
items.text: A confident event on a corridor the model gave under 10% probability is an anomaly — the model is wrong, and it says so on the map.

blocks.text: Classifier sits behind a JevClassifier interface; the real client activates the moment the key lands. Confidence is a routing signal, not a probability — below 0.6 nothing is shown, and events on low-probability corridors are flagged rather than trusted.

cues: The anomaly flag is the best idea in the system. Spend your last seconds there.
A model that announces its own misses is a model you can trust.
If asked why not a normal LLM: schema conformance is table stakes now — the honest answer is latency and cost per article at stream volume, not 'typed output'.
Do NOT say 'calibrated'. TypeSafe publishes no calibration metrics; independent testing puts it near 0.02–0.03 in-distribution and ~4x worse out of it.

slides.speaker: S3

blocks.text: The objection we designed around

Correct. So no corridor rests on seizures alone. Every edge carries a 0–100 confidence score built from six independent signals: seizures present, price gradient in the expected direction, OC Index market scores at both ends, live news hits, and cultivation upstream. Detection bias is controlled with rule of law and customs efficiency. Low-confidence corridors are drawn faint, and we say so.
Every known limitation is written into docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md §5 and docs/BLOCKERS.md, not hidden.

cues: Saying the weakness first is what makes the rest credible.
Hand off on strength: 'So — does it actually work?'

slides.speaker: S4

blocks.text: And the result that didn't go our way

items: We tested our own core hypothesis.

blocks.text: Route exposure alone does not predict a later rise in homicide or HIV once you control for vulnerability. We committed that the day we found it. Published work lands in the same place: a 2026 panel of 95 countries finds the cocaine–homicide link appears between countries but not within them — structural position on a corridor, not year-to-year flow. So being on a route is not destiny. Being on a route without services, jobs or health spending is. That is why the risk score has three columns and not one, and why this argues for harm reduction rather than interdiction.
README.md T6, committed before this slide existed · corroborated by ‘Which Illegal Markets Kill?’, European Journal on Criminal Policy and Research (2026), 95 countries, 2021–2025

cues: Deliver as strength, not apology. Eye contact, steady pace.
Key line: the effect is between countries, not within them — which is exactly what a panel model would miss.
Teams that hide null results lose to teams that report them.
If pressed on the negative sign, concede the enforcement-capacity confound before they raise it.
